title: India-EU Free Trade Agreement Will Be Game Changer, Says German Envoy
excerpt: Ambassador Jasper Wieck said the pact, expected to be signed by year-end and take effect in the first half of next year, will cut tariffs and integrate supply chains.
body:
• German Ambassador Jasper Wieck said the India-EU free trade agreement will be a game changer for bilateral trade and investment.
  • Wieck said the agreement is expected to be signed by the end of this year and enter into force in the first half of next year.
  • It would reduce tariffs on many industrial products and, partially, on agricultural products, and help integrate India-Germany supply chains.
  • Wieck spoke as India and Germany mark 75 years of diplomatic relations and 26 years of strategic partnership.

Germany's ambassador to India, Jasper Wieck, has said the proposed India-European Union free trade agreement will be a game changer for trade and investment between India and Germany, as the two countries deepen cooperation across trade, energy and strategic sectors.

Speaking to IANS on the sidelines of an event marking the 20th anniversary of the Indo-German Energy Forum in New Delhi, Wieck said the bilateral relationship is now living up to, and even surpassing, the expectations of the strategic partnership. His remarks were reported by hi INDiA.

"The EU free trade agreement, which is to be signed at the end of this year and is expected to enter into force in the first half of next year, will be a game changer for our bilateral trade and investment partnership."

— Jasper Wieck, German Ambassador to India

Tariff cuts and supply chains

Wieck said the agreement would reduce tariffs on many industrial products and, partially, on agricultural products. He said the two countries have the potential to integrate their supply chains, allowing them to use each other's capabilities for more competitive manufacturing.

A separate account of Wieck's remarks by Daily Kiran said the FTA is projected to bolster India's economy, increase government revenue and create new job opportunities, and that better supply-chain integration would also benefit exports to other countries.

Wieck's predecessor, Philipp Ackermann, made a similar assessment in July, telling ANI the agreement would be a game changer in many ways, leading to more German investment in India and possibly more Indian investment in Germany, as reducing tariffs and other barriers activates trade and investment.

Energy partnership alongside trade

Wieck underlined Germany's long-standing support for India's clean-energy ambitions, referring to the Indo-German Energy Forum, established to support India's transition from fossil fuels to renewable sources. Daily Kiran reported Wieck noting that India's renewable energy capacity has grown from approximately 2-3 gigawatts in 2006 to around 300 gigawatts today, and that the partnership will expand toward developing industrial capacity for renewable-energy equipment in India.

"We have just celebrated 75 years of diplomatic relations between India and Germany, and we have had a strategic partnership for 26 years," Wieck said, according to the IANS report. "I think we are now living up to the expectations of this strategic partnership and going beyond them."

For exporters and manufacturers, the timeline Wieck outlined — signing by the end of this year, with entry into force in the first half of next year — is the key detail to watch, as tariff schedules and implementation rules will determine which sectors benefit first.
